column3: NASB puts the aside in parentheses and renders “rules over the man” as “has jurisdiction over a person.”
NASB renders “has been cleared” as “is released” and adds “concerning.”
NASB reorders the verse and renders “which not to be her” as “so that she is not.”
NASB renders “were put to death” as “were made to die” and “belong to” as “be joined to.”
NASB renders “the passions of sins” as “the sinful passions,” adds “aroused,” and adds “of our body.”
NASB adds “by.”
NASB renders “But” as “On the contrary” and “covetousness” as “coveting”; the quotation is in capitals.
NASB renders “an occasion” as “opportunity” and “all covetousness” as “coveting of every kind.”
NASB moves “and I died,” which begins v. 10 in the Greek, into this verse; “revived” is rendered “became alive.”
NASB begins after the words moved to v. 9 and adds “to result.”
NASB renders “put me to death” as “killed me.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text (“became”); it adds “a cause of” and renders “beyond excess” as “utterly.”
NASB follows the critical text (“of flesh”); “sold under sin” is rendered “sold into bondage to sin.”
NASB renders “what I want” as “what I would like to do.”
NASB adds “confessing.”
NASB renders “dwelling” as “indwells.”
NASB follows the critical text without “I find”; it renders the last clause as “the doing of the good is not.”
Close to the Greek.
Close to the Greek.
NASB reorders the verse.
NASB renders “delight in” as “joyfully concur with” and “inward” as “inner.”
NASB renders “another” as “a different,” adds “of my body,” and renders “making captive” as “making me a prisoner.”
NASB renders “deliver” as “set free.”
NASB follows the critical text (“Thanks be to God”); it adds “on the one hand … on the other.”
